question:
A group of students investigates how changing the coefficients of an objective function can affect the optimal solution of a fixed linear programming problem. The restrictions are $x+y\leq 8$, $2x+y\leq 12$, $x\geq 0$ and $y\geq 0$. After plotting the boundary lines, the students obtain the corner points $O(0,0)$, $A(6,0)$, $B(4,4)$ and $C(0,8)$. They consider the objective function $Z=px+qy$, where $p>0$ and $q>0$. They want to determine a relation between $p$ and $q$ for which the two adjacent corner points $B$ and $C$ give the same highest value of the objective function.

(a) Write the value of $Z$ at each of the four corner points.

(b) Determine the relation between $p$ and $q$ for which $Z$ has equal values at $B$ and $C$.

(c) Under the relation obtained in part (b), verify that the common value at $B$ and $C$ is greater than the values at $O$ and $A$.

(d) Show that every point on the line segment joining $B$ and $C$ gives the same maximum value of $Z$.
explanation:
(a)
The objective function is $Z=px+qy$. Therefore,

At $O(0,0)$,
$$Z_O=0$$
At $A(6,0)$,
$$Z_A=6p$$
At $B(4,4)$,
$$Z_B=4p+4q$$
At $C(0,8)$,
$$Z_C=8q$$

(b)
For equal values at $B$ and $C$, require
$$4p+4q=8q$$
Therefore,
$$4p=4q$$
Hence,
$$p=q$$

(c)
Let $p=q$, with $p>0$. Then
$$Z_B=4p+4p=8p$$
and
$$Z_C=8p$$

At $A$, $Z_A=6p$, and at $O$, $Z_O=0$. Since $p>0$,
$$8p>6p>0$$
Thus, $B$ and $C$ both give the greatest value, namely $8p$.

(d)
The points $B(4,4)$ and $C(0,8)$ lie on the boundary line
$$x+y=8$$
Every point on the line segment $BC$ therefore satisfies $x+y=8$. Since $p=q$, the objective function becomes
$$Z=p(x+y)$$
Hence, for every point on $BC$,
$$Z=p(8)=8p$$
Thus every point on the segment joining $B$ and $C$ gives the same maximum value $8p$.

options.A:
(a) $Z_O=0$, $Z_A=6p$, $Z_B=4p+4q$, $Z_C=8q$
(b) $p=2q$
(c) The common value is $12q$ and exceeds the other values
(d) Only $B$ and $C$ are optimal
options.B:
(a) $Z_O=0$, $Z_A=6p$, $Z_B=4p+4q$, $Z_C=8q$
(b) $p=q$
(c) $Z_B=Z_C=8p>6p=Z_A$
(d) Only the endpoints $B$ and $C$ give the maximum value
options.C:
(a) $Z_O=0$, $Z_A=6q$, $Z_B=4p+4q$, $Z_C=8p$
(b) $p=q$
(c) The common maximum is $6p$
(d) Every point on $OA$ is optimal
options.D:
(a) $Z_O=0$, $Z_A=6p$, $Z_B=4p+4q$, $Z_C=8q$
(b) $p=q$
(c) $Z_B=Z_C=8p>6p=Z_A>Z_O$
(d) Every point on segment $BC$ gives the same maximum value $8p$
